## Paper

Deferred Acceptance Algorithms: History, Theory, Practice, and Open Questions

## World

labor_market

## Institution

Deferred-acceptance mechanism design.

## Agent type

Two-sided matching participants.

## Theoretical benchmark

DA properties depend on which side proposes and on preference/information assumptions.

## Learning setup

Learning/reporting agents operate within an explicitly side-proposing matching protocol.

## Metrics

Stability, match rate, truthfulness, manipulation gain, welfare.

## Main result

The deferred acceptance algorithm produces stable matchings that are optimal for one side (man-optimal or woman-optimal) and weakly Pareto optimal for the other side. The set of unmatched men and women is the same at every stable matching.

## What they prove

The set of unmatched men and women is the same at every stable matching; the man-optimal stable matching is weakly Pareto optimal for men; the woman-optimal stable matching is weakly Pareto optimal for women

## What they only simulate

Empirical evidence from labor market clearinghouses and school choice systems; effects of stable and unstable clearinghouses

## What they do NOT test

Theoretical generalizations beyond the marriage model; non-strict preferences in applications to school choice

## What we need to reproduce
